d.d: To press lightly in a repetitive motion with a soft object without rubbing.
d.x: I dabbed my face with a towel.

d.d: To apply a substance in this way.
d.x: The nurse will dab some ointment on that gash.

d.d: To strike by a thrust; to hit with a sudden blow or thrust.
A soft tap or blow; a blow or peck from a bird's beak; an aimed blow.
A soft, playful box given in greeting or approval.
A small amount, a blob of some soft or wet substance.
With a dab, or sudden contact.

present participle and gerund of dab
The act by which something is dabbed.
To make slightly wet or soiled by spattering or sprinkling a liquid (such as water, mud, or paint) on it; to bedabble.
To cause splashing by moving a body part like a bill or limb in soft mud, water, etc., often playfully; to play in shallow water; to paddle.
d.x: The children sat on the dock and dabbled their feet in the water.

d.d: To feed without diving, by submerging the head and neck underwater to seek food, often also tipping up the tail straight upwards above the water.
A spattering or sprinkling of a liquid.
An act of splashing in soft mud, water, etc.
An act of participation in an activity in a casual or superficial way.
Characterized by spots (used especially of animals and plants); dappled.
